repository.name: @webex/internal-plugin-encryption
repository.purpose: Internal plugin registered as webex.internal.encryption that encrypts and decrypts Webex content with keys held by the Key Management Service (KMS). Encryption wraps text and binary data as JWE and files as SCRs, fetches each key from KMS once, and caches it, private key material included, in the SDK unbounded storage. Its child webex.internal.encryption.kms negotiates an ECDH session with KMS, wraps every KMS request (resources, authorizations, unbound keys, customer master keys), batches the requests to the encryption service, and matches the responses that arrive as Mercury encryption.kms_message events. Before negotiating, it validates the KMS static key: the mandatory key checks always run, and certificate-chain trust is checked only when shouldValidateKMSCertificate is true, against configured roots or the signed Cisco Union bundle shipped in assets/. Optional report-only checks only emit metrics. Registered payload transforms wrap outbound kmsMessage bodies, unwrap inbound ones, and turn DRY error responses into DryError. KMS failures reject with KmsError, KmsTimeoutError, or KMSError.

public_interfaces.name: @webex/internal-plugin-encryption package entry
public_interfaces.notes: Importing the package imports the device and mercury plugins and registers Encryption as internal plugin 'encryption' with its config, the encryptKmsMessage, decryptKmsMessage, and decryptErrorResponse payload transforms, and, when NODE_ENV is test, KmsDryErrorInterceptor. The first registration of the name wins.

public_interfaces.name: webex.internal.encryption methods
public_interfaces.notes: getKey reads the unbounded storage first and caches fetched keys with private JWK material; options.onBehalfOf fetches keys for another user and needs the spark.kms_orgagent role; download falls back to the original URL when the files service lookup fails.

public_interfaces.name: webex.internal.encryption.kms methods
public_interfaces.audience: workspace plugins and BYOK administration callers
public_interfaces.notes: Every request awaits mercury.connect and a negotiated ECDH context, is batched to the encryption service, and settles from the Mercury response or a timeout. KMS errors reject with KmsError, timeouts with KmsTimeoutError, certificate failures with KMSError (which also triggers client:InvalidRequestError).

public_interfaces.name: encryption config
public_interfaces.notes: Timeouts, batching, JOSE options, and KMS certificate validation: shouldValidateKMSCertificate (default false), caroots, carootsAsset, assetsBaseUrl, reportOnlyAssetsBaseUrl, carootsReportOnly.

public_interfaces.name: package scripts
public_interfaces.notes: build runs build:src, which writes dist and runs build:assets to copy assets into dist/assets. test:unit imports dist, so build:src runs first. test:integration and test:browser need the CI test-user secrets. assets:refresh updates the shipped Union bundle. The aggregate test script chains all four test scripts and is deliberately not a manifest command.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not call the encryption service or KMS directly; go through kms.request.
negative_guidance.why: It owns Mercury, the ECDH context, wrapping, batching, and retries (INV-005).

negative_guidance.rule: Do not make enforced certificate validation succeed without verified roots, and do not let report-only checks reject.
Do not edit src/union-bundle.js or rename the asset by hand.
negative_guidance.why: The filename and rollback floor are generated together (INV-007).

negative_guidance.rule: Do not log keys, JWKs, plaintext, bearer tokens, or decrypted KMS bodies.
negative_guidance.why: They grant access to encrypted content.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not mutate the cached KMS context for an onBehalfOf request.
Do not trust a test:unit result from an outdated install.
negative_guidance.why: The pinned asn1js and pkijs and the kms-caroots link are missing there, and 18 asset cases fail for that reason.

negative_guidance.rule: Do not infer a coverage threshold for this package.
negative_guidance.why: No coverage script or threshold exists.

high.expectation: Source and a unit case agree, as for certificate validation, the CA-roots policy, fetchKey, and the CMK requests.

medium.expectation: Only source or integration evidence exists, as for batching, retries, the transforms, and the content-crypto methods. Pin current behavior with a unit case before modifying.

low.expectation: Neither source, tests, nor a dependency's spec or code settles the question, as for why the context expires 30 seconds early or why KMS details failures stay cached. Stop and report the gap.
